title: Add metadata for diagrams
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

Adds title and descriptions and examples to all diagrams, so that tools like mermaid.live, editor plugins, etc can use examples provided by diagram authors rather than maintaining a different copy, which will have to be updated manually whenever there is a new diagram in mermaid. 

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

Examples is an array, to facilitate adding different ones if the author wishes to.

### :clipboard: Tasks

Make sure you

- [ ] :book: have read the [contribution guidelines](https://mermaid.js.org/community/contributing.html)
- [ ] :computer: have added necessary unit/e2e tests.
- [ ] :notebook: have added documentation. Make sure [`MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION`](https://mermaid.js.org/community/contributing.html#update-documentation) is used for all new features.
- [ ] :butterfly: If your PR makes a change that should be noted in one or more packages' changelogs, generate a changeset by running `pnpm changeset` and following the prompts. Changesets that add features should be `minor` and those that fix bugs should be `patch`. Please prefix changeset messages with `feat:`, `fix:`, or `chore:`.
author: sidharthv96

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
**suggestion(non-blocking)**: I think this is a good enough for a v1, but I would much rather store the examples as `.mmd` files instead (or even in `.md` files).

That way, us developers get to use syntax highlighting and Mermaid plugins in the IDE when using these examples.

Maybe a structure could work something like the following?

We have an `index.ts` file with the metadata, then a `default.mmd` file with the default diagram and all the other examples can have `xxxx.mmd` file names.

```diff
diff --git a/architecture/default.mmd b/architecture/default.mmd
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..8ea7afd46
--- /dev/null
+++ b/architecture/default.mmd
@@ -0,0 +1,14 @@
+---
+title: Basic System Architecture
+---
+architecture-beta
+    group api(cloud)[API]
+
+    service db(database)[Database] in api
+    service disk1(disk)[Storage] in api
+    service disk2(disk)[Storage] in api
+    service server(server)[Server] in api
+
+    db:L -- R:server
+    disk1:T -- B:server
+    disk2:T -- B:db
diff --git a/architecture/index.ts b/architecture/index.ts
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..5ab821ea9
--- /dev/null
+++ b/architecture/index.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,7 @@
+export default {
+  name: 'Architecture Diagram',
+  description: 'Visualize system architecture and components',
+  examples: [
+    // add some cool Vite script here to automatically load them from the `.mmd` file
+  ]
+};
```

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: Will check esbuild and vite loaders for markdown.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
> esbuild and vite loaders

You can just do a `?raw` import in Vite to import the `.mmd` as a string. And it should bundlify into the exact same bundle.

Having it in a markdown file would be even cooler, but then you'd have to parse it to ensure it's exactly in the correct format, e.g.

````markdown
# Diagram Name

Diagram Description goes Here

## Examples

### Example Name Here (maybe the default one is the first one?)

Optional Example Description Here

```mermaid
info
    %% My example here
```
### Second Example Name Here

Optional example description here

```mermaid
info
    %% My second example here
```
````

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests storing examples as .mmd files instead of .ts files, with a concrete diff showing how to restructure.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
**nitpick**: I don't think we should be using `NodeNext`.

The TypeScript v5.8 (the latest version) has changed `module: "NodeNext"` to no longer be the same as `module: "Node16"` and there's now a new `modue: "Node18"` setting.

Could we switch this too:

```suggestion
    "module": "Node16",
    "moduleResolution": "Node16"
```

or to:

```suggestion
    "module": "Node18",
    "moduleResolution": "Node16"
```

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests switching from NodeNext to Node16 or Node18 with specific code suggestions.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
I think this should be split into two separate changesets.

Otherwise, the following message would appear both in the `@mermaid-js/examples` release notes/`CHANGELOG.md` and the `mermaid` release notes.

But I think you'd rather want to have the first line only in the `@mermaid-js/examples` and the second line only in the `mermaid` release notes.

comments.author: sidharthv96
aloisklink
comments.body:
> @aloisklink why don't we lock the package versions of mermaid & @mermaid-js/examples?

Hmmmm, you mean if you have version `11.7.0` of `mermaid`, you want the `@mermaid-js/examples` version to also be `11.7.0`?

The problem is that there wouldn't be a warning if you install `mermaid: "11.7.0"` and `@mermaid-js/examples: "11.8.1-different-version"`, unless `@mermaid-js/examples` has a `peerDependencies` field on `mermaid`.

But each time you make `peerDependencies` stricter, you're supposed to do a major version bump of `@mermaid-js/examples` (and I believe that's what changesets will do for us automatically if we use a `peerDependencies`).

Maybe we could instead have a `peerDependencies: {mermaid: "~11.7.0"}`? If it's the `~` specifier, then we could do patch changes to `mermaid` without bumping `@mermaid-js/examples`, but minor changes would publish a new version, even if it's a no-op?

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests adding a peerDependency on Mermaid in package.json.

comments.body:

I think I'd slightly prefer a `1.0.0` release, just so we know that `minor` = `feat`, but that's up to you.
